# Command line

::: {.doc-lead}
Inspect projects, make precise edits, and export work from a terminal.
:::

Scripts and agents can work on the same project as the app. Flux ships three programmatic
surfaces over one shared core:

- **The `flux` CLI** — around a hundred typed commands ("verbs") that operate on a project's
  files directly: compose figures, restyle plot parts, manage references, compile the
  manuscript, build slide decks.
- **The MCP server** — the same verbs exposed as typed tools for AI agents, plus a few
  agent-only niceties (inline figure PNGs so an agent can *look* at its work).
- **The live bridge** — while the app is open, commands can act on the *running* GUI: read
  what you have selected, apply an edit as an undoable action you watch happen.

You never have to use any of this — the app is complete on its own. But it's what makes the
[flux-connect workflow](/docs/connect.html) possible, and it's handy for scripting.

## Invoking {#invoking}

On first run Flux creates a stable launcher at `~/.local/share/flux/bin/flux` on Linux and
macOS. Add that folder to PATH or use the full path; optional `~/.local/bin` shims delegate
to it. Then:

```bash
flux help                 # every verb, always current
flux config               # this machine's resolved paths (FluxConfig, FluxLib, …)
flux list                 # figures + references of the current project
```

Commands find their project as: an explicit `--root`, else the `FLUX_PROJECT` environment
variable, else the current directory. `cd` into a project (or export `FLUX_PROJECT`) and go.

## Connect an agent {#connect-an-agent}

Run `flux connect /path/to/project` in the agent's shell, or invoke its installed
flux-connect skill. The command returns the reading plan for a pack; the agent reads
it, views its images, returns a receipt and waits for your request. `global` connects
without choosing a project; `--refresh`, `--depth full` and `--live` control refresh,
reading depth and live pairing. [Connect an agent](/docs/connect.html)
explains setup and the receipt.

## Common tasks {#a-taste}

The installed app includes the PNG renderer used by the CLI and MCP. An agent can
view figures and canvas overviews without a source checkout or a separate renderer install.

```bash
# Compose plots into one labeled multi-panel figure, then render it to look at
flux compose-figure plots/*.svg --id fig1 --rows 2
flux render-figure fig1 --png --out /tmp/fig1.png

# Restyle one part, or a whole series and its legend swatch (both survive regeneration)
flux restyle fig1 control.line --stroke '#205EA6'
flux set-series-color fig1 control '#205EA6'

# Read the plot's data: exact x/y, bins, statistics and brackets
flux get-plot-data fig1 --series control --limit 50

# Add a reference to the project, then compile the manuscript with Quarto
flux cite-doi 10.1038/nature12373
flux compile --to pdf
```

Edits made headless show up **live** in the open app, and if you're mid-edit in the app when a
command arrives, it defers politely instead of clobbering ([saving and outside
edits](/docs/projects-and-files.html#saving)).

## Full command reference {#command-reference}

The [CLI and MCP command reference](/docs/commands.html) lists the project, figure, plot, document, library, slide and agent commands for the Flux version this site documents.

Use `flux help` for the list in your installed version, or `flux help <verb>` for a command's flags. `flux version` identifies the installation. The same reference is available locally in `FluxConfig/Context/FluxContext/CLI-REFERENCE.md`.

For example, `flux help read-log` prints:

```text
  read-log [--tail <value>] [--since-checkpoint] [--titles] [--json] [--root R]
      Read the project Log: the latest entries, from the latest checkpoint, or titles only.
```

## Connecting an MCP client {#connecting-an-mcp-client}

Point an MCP client at the [launcher](/docs/cli.html#invoking) with `args = ["mcp"]`; add a
project path after `mcp` for a fixed default. The optional `~/.local/bin/flux` and
`flux-connect` shims delegate to the same launcher. On Windows the launcher is
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\flux\bin\flux.cmd`, although Windows does not yet have a supported
[installer](/install/).

`flux mcp` starts with the compact `core` toolset. Use `flux_verbs` to discover
commands and `flux_verb` to run them, or `flux mcp --toolset full` for every dedicated
tool. Ask the agent for `flux-connect /path/to/project` to bind it. Finding a
project from cwd only supplies a default for tools; it does not load context.
Project tools can also take a `project` argument for one call.

Relative filesystem inputs use the shell cwd on the CLI and the project root over
MCP. Absolute paths are honoured. Document identifiers remain project-relative.

## Agent setup and diagnostics {#agent-setup-and-diagnostics}

`flux connect setup --dry-run` previews installation. Apply with `flux connect setup`;
`--agents claude,codex` selects vendors, `--yes` confirms replacing an existing Flux
registration, and `--create-local-bin` creates the optional convenience shims.
Flux prints the macOS PATH instruction; it never edits shell startup files.

`flux connect doctor` checks the launcher, full MCP handshake, PNG rendering,
context files, published skills, hooks, registrations and known projects.
`--json` returns the same checks as the read-only MCP tool `connect_doctor`.
Setup and removal are CLI actions and cannot be invoked over MCP.

On Windows, setup registers the pinned runtime and CLI script directly; MCP
hosts do not have to execute a `.cmd` shim. Run setup again after relocating Flux.

## Troubleshooting {#troubleshooting}

Use `flux connect doctor` for launcher, tools and integration errors. After moving an
installation, rerun setup and restart agent sessions. A missing `flux` command usually
means the launcher directory is not on PATH; use its full path above.
